subject: Recap: API portability & next steps (migration off proprietary LLM APIs)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alice Byrne <alice.byrne@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: API portability & next steps (migration off proprietary LLM APIs)

Hi Alice — thanks again for the intro call today. Wanted to capture what we discussed and confirm next steps so we’re aligned. Short recap below.

Summary of pain / goals
- Cost & rate limits: OpenAI spend is the biggest line item today; spikes during peak hours cause throttling and delayed UX.
- Vendor lock & portability: engineering wants the ability to move away from a single proprietary API without a full rewrite (function/tool-calling, embedding compatibility).
- Compliance & audit: data residency, audit logs, and KMS are non-negotiable for your regulated workflows.
- Latency sensitivity: core support flows require P95 <= 200ms for short (<=64 token) answers.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Text gen: OpenAI (gpt-4o/gpt-4o-mini for prod), ~70% of calls.
- Safety/classification: Anthropic for classification/safety checks on outputs.
- Embeddings: OpenAI embeddings powering search/ranking.
- Orchestration: internal microservices + Lambda-backed tool calls (Zendesk & internal CRM integrations via webhooks).

Success criteria for a migration/POC
1) Feature parity: tool/function calling, streaming, structured JSON output, and safety/classification hooks.
2) Embedding parity: similar vector quality and compatibility with current ranking pipeline.
3) Cost target: 40–60% reduction in per-token unit costs based on estimated workload.
4) Security/compliance: VPC/private deployment option, KMS integration, and audit log retention (90 days+).
5) Performance: maintain or improve current P95 latency for short responses.

Model shortlist (initial candidates we recommend for evaluation)
- Llama 2 / Meta family (13B chat variant) — good instruction-following baseline.
- Falcon-40B-Instruct — strong on instruction tasks; may need quantization tuning.
- Mistral-Instruct / Mistral 7B mixtures — good inference efficiency for chat.
- Mosaic MPT-7B-Chat — flexible and efficient for embeddings when tuned.

Immediate next steps (agreed)
- Redwood: deliver a POC plan + cost estimate and recommended model mapping for your top 3 flows (support replies, triage classification, search embeddings) — target by Fri 2026-05-01.
- Acme Health: provide a small prompt set (10–15 representative prompts per flow) and a 48-hour sample of request volume for footprinting.
- Kickoff POC: propose Wed 2026-05-05 for a technical kickoff (30–45m).

Attachments included: acme-mutual-action-plan.pdf (mutual action plan stub), redwood-objective-checklist.xlsx (POC objective checklist).

If I missed anything or you want changes to the success criteria, let me know — otherwise I’ll circulate a short POC plan and model-cost snapshot by Friday.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Recap: API portability & next steps (migration off proprietary LLM APIs)

Folks — forwarding the external recap to loop you in. Short internal asks below so we can meet the Friday timeline.

Rishi: can you run a back-of-envelope cost & perf estimate for the four candidate models across their typical dev/prod quantization options? Focus on: token cost, expected GPU throughput (tokens/sec), and inference cost for our Dedicated offering. Target: initial numbers by Thu EOD (2026-04-30).

Monica: please pull the compliance checklist items that map to Acme’s requirements (VPC, KMS, audit retention) and confirm which artifacts we can share for the POC. Also flag any gaps that would require Private deployment instead of Hosted.

Action items (owners & due dates)
- Model-performance snapshot (Rishi) — 2026-04-30
- Compliance artifact list + redlines (Monica) — 2026-04-30
- Draft POC plan and mutual action plan (Soojin) — 2026-05-01

Call notes: they highlighted two tricky points: (1) tool-calling via Lambdas must be preserved without changing their tooling significantly, and (2) their safety/classification pipeline must be pluggable (they may want to keep Anthropic for classification).

Ping me if you want to talk through any of the flows — I’m booking 30m slots Thu/ Fri afternoon for prep.

— Soojin

[Forwarded message below]

From: Alice Byrne <alice.byrne@acmehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: EngOps Team <eng-ops@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Apr 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: API portability & next steps (migration off proprietary LLM APIs)

Thanks Soojin — this is perfect and covers everything we discussed. A few clarifications from my side: 
- Usage split: ~70% OpenAI for generation, ~20% Anthropic for classification, ~10% other.
- Tooling: our Lambda-based tool-calls are critical; we cannot move to any solution that requires re-architecting the majority of our webhooks. If Redwood can support the same function-call pattern (HTTP -> Lambda) during the POC, that would be ideal.
- Embedding expectations: we need embeddings to play nicely with our existing vector DB (we use Pinecone today). If you can validate top-k recall parity on the sample prompt set, that will be the key gating criteria.

We’ll assemble the prompt sets and the 48-hour sample traffic dump by EOD Thu (2026-04-30). Wed 2026-05-05 for a kickoff works for our eng lead (10–11am PT) — please send a calendar invite.

Minor ask: include a short section in the POC plan that outlines rollback criteria (what would cause us to pause the POC) — primarily around regression in latency or drop in top-k retrieval quality.

Looking forward to the POC plan.

Best,
Alice Byrne
Head of Machine Intelligence, Acme Health
